course_name_original: Técnicas de Expresión Oral y Escrita en Inglés
course_name_en: Oral and Written Expression Techniques in English
prerequisites: Prior knowledge of English grammatical and linguistic structures and a communicative competence at B2 level, according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

learning_outcomes.text: Follow and give simple oral presentations, making correct use of intonation and expressive possibilities.
Request and offer services related to the work environment, using varied, precise, and appropriate vocabulary for the situation.
Participate in meetings and seminars by taking notes, presenting own ideas, and making proposals.
Handle routine requests for goods or services over the phone.
Draft and understand formal reports and routine professional correspondence according to established rhetorical, grammatical, and lexical rules.

syllabus_topics: Drafting professional documentation: Use of formal email conventions
Preparation of technical reports: structure and linguistic characteristics
Participating in socio-professional activities within the company: Conducting job interviews and presenting CVs
Participating in debates, meetings, and negotiations
Use of language and linguistic signaling techniques
Use of visual aids and body language
Use of voice: rhythm and emphasis
teaching_methods: Use of written and audio materials

assessment_methods.method: Individual written exam on a cover letter (E1)
Individual oral exam on a simulated job interview (E2)
Individual written exam on the technical report's linguistic aspects and content (E3)
Individual oral presentation on technological innovation (E5)

assessment_rules: The final grade for the ordinary call is calculated as: E1 + T1 + E2 + T2 + E3 + E4 + E5 + E6 + C1. To pass the course, a grade equal to or greater than 5 must be obtained. There will be no final exam for the ordinary call. For extraordinary calls, students take a theoretical and a practical exam, composed of several parts; grades from the ordinary call are not retained. The final grade is calculated as P1+P2+P3+P4+T1. To pass, a grade equal to or greater than 5 must be obtained.
